definition: Answering questions that require chaining evidence across documents ("who managed the project that replaced system X?") through iterative retrieve-reason-retrieve cycles instead of one lookup.
details: Answering questions that require chaining evidence across documents ("who managed the project that replaced system X?") through iterative retrieve-reason-retrieve cycles instead of one lookup.

explainer.lead: Multi-hop retrieval answers questions that require chaining evidence across documents through iterative retrieve-reason-retrieve cycles instead of a single lookup. It matters for questions like who managed the project that replaced system X, where no one document holds the answer.

tiers.eli5: It's like following a chain of clues: you look something up, learn a new name, then look that name up, and repeat until you have the answer. One search alone wouldn't get you there.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers implement it as iterative retrieve-reason-retrieve cycles so each lookup informs the next. A single one-shot lookup is insufficient when evidence must be chained across documents.
tiers.paperLevel: Answering questions that require chaining evidence across documents through iterative retrieve-reason-retrieve cycles instead of one lookup.

explainer.example: To find who managed the project that replaced system X, the system first retrieves the replacement project, then retrieves its manager.
